reviewStatus: Drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Modified Rankin Scale

version.label: Modified Rankin Scale 0–6 (van Swieten et al. 1988)
version.detail: Standard UK-TIA wording with grade 6 (dead), as used in stroke trials. Variant wordings (e.g. adding 'neurological' to each grade) are not combined. Structured interview instruments are not reproduced.

purpose: A global measure of disability and dependence in daily activities. It describes functional status, not the severity of a neurological deficit.
intendedPopulation: Adults after stroke and other neurological conditions, typically at baseline (pre-morbid), discharge and follow-up.

calculatorNotice.title: Functional outcome scale
calculatorNotice.message: mRS grades disability and dependence in daily life. It is not a neurological severity score, and it reflects function from all causes, not only the neurological condition.

inputDefinitions.label: Functional level
inputDefinitions.help: Choose the single grade that best describes the person's current function across all activities. A structured interview improves reliability.

options.label: No significant disability despite symptoms
options.detail: Able to carry out all usual duties and activities.

options.label: Slight disability
options.detail: Unable to carry out all previous activities, but able to look after own affairs without assistance.

options.label: Moderate disability
options.detail: Requiring some help, but able to walk without assistance.

options.label: Moderately severe disability
options.detail: Unable to walk without assistance and unable to attend to own bodily needs without assistance.

options.label: Severe disability
options.detail: Bedridden, incontinent and requiring constant nursing care and attention.

resultStates.label: No symptoms
resultStates.summary: Functional status: no symptoms at all at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes function at this timepoint, not the underlying condition.

resultStates.label: No significant disability
resultStates.summary: Functional status: symptoms present; able to carry out all usual duties and activities.

resultStates.label: Slight disability
resultStates.summary: Functional status: independent in own affairs, but unable to carry out all previous activities.

resultStates.label: Moderate disability
resultStates.summary: Functional status: requires some help; walks without assistance.

resultStates.label: Moderately severe disability
resultStates.summary: Functional status: cannot walk or attend to bodily needs without assistance.

resultStates.label: Severe disability
resultStates.summary: Functional status: bedridden, incontinent, requires constant nursing care.

clinicalContext.text: Describes global disability and dependence in daily activities, from all causes.
Used to document pre-morbid function, discharge status and follow-up outcomes.
A common outcome in stroke trials, analysed either across all grades or split at a defined cut-off.

clinicalInsights.text: Record the timepoint and source (pre-morbid, discharge, follow-up; patient, carer or records). Pre-morbid mRS changes how later grades are read.
'Favourable outcome' cut-offs differ between studies (0–1, 0–2, or full ordinal shift). State the definition when comparing results.
Grades 1–3 have the most inter-rater disagreement; a structured interview improves reliability.
Grade 0 describes function at this assessment; it does not describe the underlying neurological condition.

limitations.text: Measures global disability, not neurological severity or a specific deficit.

limitations: Moderate inter-rater reliability without a structured assessment.
Weighted toward mobility and self-care; cognition, mood and communication may be under-represented.
Reflects disability from all causes, including non-neurological comorbidity.

confounders.effect: Existing dependence is included unless pre-morbid mRS is recorded.
Cardiac, respiratory or orthopaedic limits raise the grade.
Different informants may give different grades.
Function changes during recovery; grades are timepoint-specific.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The neurological deficit or its severity (see NIHSS).
Quality of life or rehabilitation potential.
commonErrors: Treating mRS as a measure of neurological severity.

guideSections.what: A 7-grade ordinal scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (dead) describing global disability and dependence.
guideSections.whenToUse: Documenting pre-morbid function, discharge status and follow-up outcomes after stroke and other neurological conditions; trial outcomes.
guideSections.howToPerform: Establish the person's usual activities and current level of help needed. Choose the single grade that best fits overall function. Record the timepoint and information source. Structured interviews improve consistency.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A functional outcome measure, used alongside measures of neurological deficit (e.g. NIHSS) rather than in place of them.

sources.citation: van Swieten JC, Koudstaal PJ, Visser MC, Schouten HJ, van Gijn J. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke. 1988;19(5):604-607.
Rankin J. Cerebral vascular accidents in patients over the age of 60. II. Prognosis. Scott Med J. 1957;2(5):200-215.

licensing.note: Structured mRS interview instruments (e.g. mRS-9Q, Rankin Focused Assessment) have their own terms and are not reproduced.
